limitations: Dataset baselines are the original2005 SDSS scene-model reduced source labelled5.04, the later pinned c447 SMPv8+BOSS reduced release, and one current archival HST GO10158 F606W RAW/engineering/association product snapshot. They are distinct products and reduction histories, not a joint independent-data model.

HST count payloads are acquired and their declared header/layout checked; image values and engineering telemetry are unanalysed. Counts do not establish electrons, QE, photon/readout distribution, censoring or calibrated photometry. RAW ERR/DQ encode constant-zero placeholders via NPIX1/2 and PIXVALUE, without pixel payload. They are not measured zero uncertainty or verified clean quality. Gain/read-noise/photometric zeros are not zero noise/calibration uncertainty.

Current CALACS10.4.1 processing log and DrizzlePac3.11.0 association metadata do not identify or reproduce the source paper2010 PSF/dust/lens-light/potential/drizzle processing. Only one of four ASN exposures is locally acquired; full F606W/F814W imaging and calibrated products, reference bodies, PSF ensembles/masks/image covariance remain unacquired.

Literal legacyCID6057→epoch→RUN5566/82N is now checked, and a separate c447 HEAD row declares allCandidates PHOT pointers. Physical event deduplication, legacy→SMPv8 reduction/flux/error equivalence, camcol/field/native exposure, per-epoch clock standard, exposure/readout operator, sky/calibration/QE and full selection bridge remain unresolved. HST assets cannot substitute for SDSS.

The old Suyu paper identity/selected-source review remains ancestry: printed November26,2024 draft header versus January28,2010 v2 watermark stays unresolved, and older WFPC2 GO6555 is distinct. Radio time series/joint delay covariance, Keck spectra/templates/aperture/seeing, environment selection/simulated sightlines and their joint likelihood remain unacquired.

Pixel, extraction, calibration, delay, kinematic, environment and cross-probe covariances/distributions remain unknown, not zero or Gaussian/Poisson. Error components, read-noise/gain metadata and fitted distance summaries do not supply a measured physical law or physical history.
